It is a scam when the caller does any of these: asks for an OTP, PIN, CVV, password or card number; asks to install an app (AnyDesk, QuickSupport, a "support" or "KYC" app) or to share the screen; asks to send money, pay a "fine", "fee", "deposit" or "verification amount", or to move money to a "safe" or "RBI" account; threatens arrest, a case, a frozen account, a blocked SIM or a seized parcel; says to keep it secret or to stay on a video call; claims to be police, CBI, customs, TRAI, a court, a bank or a boss, and then asks for any of the above; offers a prize, refund, job or investment that needs money first. Signs from the owner's side: "should I tell the OTP", "which app should I download", "where should I send the money", "I haven't done anything", reading digits out.

It is NOT a scam when a real bank, courier, police officer or family member only informs, confirms an appointment or delivery, or warns about fraud, and never asks for an OTP, PIN, app, money or secrecy. A delivery agent asking for a delivery OTP for a parcel the person ordered is normal. Talk about scams (news, a warning) is not a scam.
